model_organism.citation: Extended lifespan and reduced adiposity in mice lacking the FAT10 gene (PMID: 24706839)
phenotypes: preferential use of fat as fuel
increased AMP kinase activity in skeletal muscle
decreased triglyceride content in skeletal muscle
enhanced insulin sensitivity in metabolic tissues
elevated IL-10 in skeletal muscle and serum

model_organism.citation: The ubiquitin-like modifier FAT10 is not essential for MHC-I antigen presentation (PMID: 40821782)
phenotypes: no effect on MHC-I surface expression
no effect on generation of endogenous MHC-I epitopes
no effect on generation of virus-derived MHC-I epitopes
unchanged cytotoxic T cell response to viruses compared to wild-type

biological.citation: Single-cell profiling reveals immune disturbances landscape and HLA-F-mediated immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface in preeclampsia (PMID: 37854606)
biological.summary: HLA-F overexpression in Jar trophoblast cells promoted cell proliferation, invasion, and migration, while underexpression had opposite effects. In NK-92MI cells, HLA-F overexpression increased secretion of immunoregulatory cytokines (CSF1, CCL22) and promoted adaptive NKG2C+ NK cell transformation.

biological.citation: HLA-F regulates the proliferation of trophoblast via PKM2-dependent glycolysis in the pathogenesis of preeclampsia (PMID: 40251569)
biological.summary: HLA-F regulates trophoblast proliferation through PKM2-dependent glycolysis. HLA-F binds the PKM promoter to regulate PKM2 transcription and promotes PKM2 enzyme activity by downregulating lactylation at K305 residue, enhancing glycolytic flux and cell proliferation.

HLA-F is a non-classical oligomorphic HLA molecule expressed on trophoblasts at the maternal-fetal interface. It participates in KIR-HLA interactions with decidual NK cells, contributing to immune recognition and tolerance of the semi-allogeneic fetus.

biological.citation: A role for both HLA-F and HLA-G in reproduction and during pregnancy? (PMID: 31558330)
biological.summary: HLA-F can be expressed as open conformers binding multiple KIRs on NK cells, and as peptide-bound HLA-F binding to inhibitory receptors ILT2 and ILT4. HLA-F has potential roles in viral infections, cancer immunology, and fertility/reproduction.

biological.citation: The involvement of HLA-E and -F in pregnancy (PMID: 16487601)
biological.summary: HLA-F is expressed on the surface of extravillous trophoblast that has invaded the maternal decidua, a unique expression site in human development. HLA-F likely contributes collectively with HLA-E and HLA-G to enable fetal development through receptor-ligand interactions.

biological.citation: HLA-F transcriptional and protein differential expression according to its genetic polymorphisms (PMID: 37166140)
biological.summary: HLA-F mRNA is detected in most cell types with protein localized in ER and Golgi apparatus. HLA-F reaches the membrane upon activation of primary cells and cell lines. SNPs rs1362126, rs2523405, and rs2523393 in HLA-F-AS1 region are associated with HLA-F mRNA expression with double-dose effects.

biological.citation: HLA Class Ib-receptor interactions during embryo implantation and early pregnancy (PMID: 35234898)
biological.summary: HLA-F interacts with inhibitory/activating ILT2 and ILT4 receptors and KIRs on uterine NK cells. HLA-F fluctuates during the menstrual cycle with high levels during the implantation window, and its expression correlates with CD56+ NK cell numbers in mid-secretory endometrium.

biological.citation: Tetrameric complexes of HLA-E, HLA-F, and HLA-G (PMID: 12213342)
biological.summary: HLA-F tetrameric complexes bind to ILT2 and ILT4 receptors on immune cells, demonstrating direct receptor-ligand interactions. This methodology enabled identification of HLA-F ligands and functional characterization.

biological.citation: ASHG 2010 - Identification of multiple genetic variants related to nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition through genome-wide scan (W. Su, K. Tse, M. Yang, Y. Chang, Y. Shugart)
biological.summary: Two HLA-F SNPs (rs3129055 and rs9258122) showed significant association with nasopharyngeal carcinoma predisposition in a GWAS of 277 NPC patients and 285 controls, with p-values of 7.36×10⁻¹¹ and 3.33×10⁻¹⁰ respectively.

biological.citation: HLA-F and LILRB1 Genetic Polymorphisms Associated with Alloimmunisation in Sickle Cell Disease (PMID: 37686397)
biological.summary: HLA-F genetic polymorphisms in regulatory regions are associated with alloimmunization susceptibility in sickle cell disease patients. HLA-F polymorphisms influence protein expression levels and modulate inflammatory and immune responses through LILRB1 receptor interactions.
